status_summary: Congressional proposals point in different directions and none is enacted. S. 2202 (introduced 2025-06-27) and the Senate-reported FY2026 intelligence authorization (S. 2342, reported 2025-07-17, Sec. 406) would have transferred NCSC to the FBI. The Senate intelligence committee's FY2027 bill (S. 4615, reported 2026-05-20) would have the DNI, through the NCSC Director, seek to establish an IC counterintelligence office at the Commerce Department (Sec. 606), a widening of NCSC's outreach role, while its Sec. 601(e) would make the NCSC Director a DNI appointee rather than a presidential appointee confirmed by the Senate. Division F of Public Law 119-60 (signed 2025-12-18) made no NCSC transfer or authority expansion; its counterintelligence items include DOD briefings for service members, FBI notices on assessments of candidates and officeholders, and added NCSC coordination on the annual report about Chinese Communist Party influence operations (Sec. 6701). ODNI's August 2025 fact sheet kept NCSC and focused it on clearance reform, counterintelligence threats and leak investigations. Defense One reported on 2025-09-11, mainly from anonymous former officials, that an earlier reorganization had cut NCSC's senior leadership to one acting director and that further cuts were being weighed; ODNI did not comment. NCSC and partner agencies issued a Safeguarding Academia bulletin for universities on 2025-08-25, and a Senate-confirmed NCSC Director took office in September 2025; neither changed NCSC's authorities. The FY2026 budget request proposed about 555 million dollars less for the FBI than FY2025, but the enacted FY2026 appropriation (Public Law 119-74) was about flat at 10.62 billion dollars, with no counterintelligence-specific figure published. NPR reported on 2026-10-06, from five anonymous sources, that FBI counterintelligence squads in many field offices were at 50 to 60 percent of positions filled as staff moved to violent crime, gang and immigration work without a specific directive to cut; the FBI called the reporting false and said its counterintelligence task forces exceed 1,500 personnel. No executive order or Counterintelligence Enhancement Act update covering universities and no reinstatement of the two advisory bodies was found.

timeline.event: The Attorney General's charging memorandum disbanded the FBI-led Foreign Influence Task Force and limited criminal FARA and Section 951 charges to espionage-like conduct by foreign government actors (see c07-12).

ODNI's ODNI 2.0 fact sheet kept NCSC and focused it on security clearance reform, deterring counterintelligence threats and overseeing leak investigations (the fact sheet is undated; the date is that of the announcement).

timeline.event: Public Law 119-60 was signed; Division F includes no NCSC transfer or authority expansion, and Sec. 6701 adds NCSC coordination to the annual report on Chinese Communist Party influence operations in the United States.

The FY2026 Commerce, Justice, Science appropriations act (Public Law 119-74) funded the FBI at 10,624.5 million dollars, about flat with FY2025 (10,673.7 million) and above the request (10,118.6 million), which had proposed a cut of about 555 million dollars; no counterintelligence-specific figure is given.

The Senate intelligence committee reported S. 4615, the FY2027 intelligence authorization, whose Sec. 606 would have the DNI, through the NCSC Director, seek to establish an IC counterintelligence office at Commerce headquarters by 2028-01-01, and whose Sec. 601(e) would make the NCSC Director appointed by the DNI rather than by the President with Senate confirmation.
The Senate intelligence committee filed its written report on S. 4615 (S. Rept. 119-133); the bill remained on the Senate Legislative Calendar as Calendar No. 420.

title: Expand NCSC authorities, add FBI counterintelligence resources, revive advisory councils
uncertainties: Stage is proposed because the only step that would amplify NCSC's role (S. 4615 Sec. 606) is in an unenacted committee-reported bill; the match is partial because that office covers one department's counterintelligence support, not the Mandate's broader authorities, university coverage or advisory boards. Rule applied: diverged needs an operative action running opposite to the text. The NCSC-to-FBI transfer proposals were not enacted; ODNI kept NCSC and a Senate-confirmed Director took office in September 2025; the reported NCSC leadership and staff cuts (Defense One, 2025-09-11) and FBI counterintelligence staffing losses (NPR, 2026-10-06) rest on anonymous sources, the FBI disputes the latter, and NPR reports no directive to cut; enacted FY2026 FBI funding was about flat, so the cut in the request did not become operative. Judgment: the Attorney General's 2025-02-05 disbanding of the FBI-led Foreign Influence Task Force (see c07-12) is a narrow change to foreign-influence work and was not treated as a cut to FBI counterintelligence resources overall. Parallel activity, such as NCSC's August 2025 Safeguarding Academia bulletin and the added NCSC coordination role on a report in Sec. 6701, does not raise the stage. S. 4615 Sec. 601(e) points the other way on NCSC's standing and is also unenacted. If official figures later confirm an FBI counterintelligence reduction, or a statute or order narrows NCSC's role, diverged should be reconsidered. Division F section text on the committee page was read through Sec. 6703(e)(1)(A), where the page text ends; later sections were read by title only. In the part read, NCSC appears only in Sec. 6701 (report preparation by the NCSC Director in coordination with the FBI, CIA and NSA Directors), and the FBI counterintelligence items are Secs. 6521 and 6524. S. 4615 was read through Sec. 611. Searches for the two advisory boards found no reinstatement (a July 2026 notice renews an unrelated DoD education board), and no executive order or Counterintelligence Enhancement Act update was found. ODNI downsizing generally is covered in c07-01, which is a cross-reference, not a duplicate. BILLSTATUS records confirm S. 2202 was only referred to committee (no later action), S. 2342 was reported but never passed the Senate, and S. 4615 was reported and then had its written report filed on 2026-08-05 with no floor action.
